attacks.claim: go.mod adds `replace go.uber.org/zap => ../zap`, pointing the build at a sibling local directory outside the repo. A clean CI checkout has no ../zap, so the build fails, or it compiles unreviewed local source that bypasses go.sum verification. That code would go into the binary distributed to on-call laptops. The replace also overrides the pinned pseudo-version, so the zap bump the PR describes is never what gets built.

printPlan recomputes batches independently of computeBatches and gets them wrong. It uses floor(len(hosts)*MaxSurge) instead of ceil(len(rest)*MaxSurge), and it iterates over all hosts without removing the canary, so the canary is printed in batch 0 and again in a later batch. With 10 hosts, canary h1 and max-surge 0.25, the real run uses batches of 3 over 9 hosts while the dry-run prints batches of 2 that include the canary. The feature exists so on-call can trust this plan before an irreversible rollout.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... for i := 0; i < len(hosts); i += per  (vs computeBatches: rest = without(hosts, o.CanaryHost); size := int(math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge)))

attacks.claim: No test verifies that the dry-run output equals the batches computeBatches executes, for canary or non-canary cases. The divergence above would ship undetected. The duplicated batching logic will also drift further over time.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no *_test.go changes comparing printPlan output with computeBatches
